task: Panel-to-global phase-hull stability under omitted-phase discovery and coverage assumptions

evidence_files.status: primary source selectively read; CAL is finite-grid Bayesian hull active learning
primary v2 preprint selectively read; average error and structure-search limits
exact rational finite fixture; not proof of general results

claims.exact_statement: For a finite complete competitor universe Omega, target upper bound U_t, and certified independent lower bounds L_z on every competing phase, let H_L(x_t)=min{sum_z lambda_z L_z: lambda>=0, sum lambda=1, sum lambda x_z=x_t}. The target is stable for every allowed interval completion iff U_t<=H_L(x_t). By LP strong duality this is equivalent to an affine plane ell with ell(x_t)>=U_t and ell(x_z)<=L_z for every competitor z.
assumptions: Omega contains every admissible competing phase, including omitted structures and same-composition polymorphs.
All energies and compositions use the same per-atom thermodynamic convention, target fidelity, temperature, and pressure.
Energy uncertainty is an independent box with target upper bound U_t and competitor lower bounds L_z.
The target composition is a feasible convex combination of competitor compositions; LP arithmetic/rounding is certified.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard robust LP and convex-hull duality applied to a complete finite phase universe; not a new hull algorithm. If the LP fails, an unstable completion exists inside the supplied independent interval box, so any stronger claim needs extra information.

costs.acquisition: Must supply certified lower bounds for all competing phases or complete enumeration; this can dominate DFT/structure-search cost.
costs.runtime: One hull LP plus a primal/dual witness; polynomial in encoded finite input, excluding structure generation and energy acquisition.
costs.nature_boundary: A PBE certificate concerns PBE; experimental claims require matched Gibbs-energy intervals and model-error coverage.

claims.falsifier: A phase in Omega has energy below its claimed L_z, or a checked LP primal/dual witness violates the asserted inequalities.
claims.next_gate: Construct a verifiable omitted-phase lower-bound service for a named real chemical system and independently review the proof/implementation.

claims.exact_statement: Freeze a support plane ell with ell(x_t)>=U_t and an audit law Q over omitted phase IDs. For the alternative class where the target is unstable by at least eta and Q({z:E_z<=ell(x_z)-eta})>=rho, independent Q draws with exact energy queries or deterministic error epsilon<eta miss all detectable plane violations with probability at most (1-rho)^m. Thus m>=ceil(log(delta)/log(1-rho)) bounds false global-stable output by delta.
assumptions: The plane and Q are frozen before an independent audit; Q's support and candidate generator are declared.
Every alternative in scope has energy-depth eta and bad-set probability at least rho; this is an extra premise, not implied by instability.
Each queried energy has deterministic error at most epsilon<eta, or a separately justified detection probability is supplied.
The target energy is bounded by U_t<=ell(x_t); only alternatives satisfying the stated depth and coverage conditions are protected.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard independent-sampling miss bound applied to a plane-violation set. Does not prove a realistic materials Q has positive rho, and does not cover instability gaps below eta.

costs.DFT: m candidate-generation/relaxation/high-fidelity energy evaluations; actual core-hours and failure rates must be recorded.
costs.synthesis: With per-attempt detection floor p_min, miss bound is (1-rho*p_min)^m; charge each attempt and characterization. Failed synthesis is censored.
costs.sample_size: m=ceil(log(delta)/log(1-rho)); e.g. rho=0.01 and delta=0.05 requires 299 independent queries.

claims.falsifier: A fully enumerated blind benchmark finds Q(bad set)<rho, a claimed low phase below the detection margin is missed above delta, or measured query error violates epsilon.
claims.next_gate: Pre-register and validate rho, eta, and oracle error on a frozen, fully enumerated chemical benchmark before any global-certification claim.

claims.exact_statement: For N known IDs with exact query answers, a null with no destabilizer and an alternative that changes exactly one uniformly random ID to a deep destabilizer have transcript total variation m/N after m distinct adaptive queries. The equal-prior minimax testing error is exactly (1-m/N)/2. If stable-null certification probability is at least 1-alpha, average false-stable probability is at least (1-m/N)(1-alpha); alpha=0 and false-stable target delta require m>= (1-delta)N.
assumptions: Finite known ID universe, exact answers, and alternatives differ from the null only at the hidden ID.
Hidden ID is uniform for the average-case statement; the one-sided certificate bound averages over this prior.
No structural lower bound or informative prior over candidate IDs is supplied.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary oracle indistinguishability bound, not materials-specific discovery evidence. It applies equally to CAL/GNoME when given identical oracle information and no valid prior/lower-bound service.

costs.distinct_queries: For N=10000 and delta=0.05, at least 9500 distinct DFT candidate evaluations are needed under the alpha=0 guarantee.
costs.with_replacement: One hidden ID has miss probability (1-1/N)^m; approximately N*log(1/delta) queries are required.

claims.falsifier: A proposed algorithm with the stated exact-oracle information beats m/N detection on the registered uniform hidden-ID benchmark; this would indicate extra information or an implementation error.
claims.next_gate: Run equal-information query-ranking benchmark with CAL, GNoME-style ranking, uniform random, and the exact lower-bound oracle.

claims.exact_statement: A denominator-M grid of normalized compositions over q elements contains binom(M+q-1,q-1) points; with S candidate structures per composition it has S*binom(M+q-1,q-1) IDs. Under a global L-Lipschitz phase-family residual and instability depth eta, an eta/(2L)-net detects a plane violation of depth at least eta/2 in every family; with family weight w_min and composition density q_min, a random radius-eta/(2L) hit has mass at least w_min*q_min*c_q*(eta/(2L))^(q-1), where c_q is a domain ball-volume lower bound.
assumptions: Phase structure families have globally Lipschitz energy residuals across the simplex; isolated stoichiometric phases may violate this premise.
A deterministic net covers every family, or the random audit law has family-weight and density lower bounds.
For sampled eta/2-depth violations, query error is below eta/2.
claims.novelty_boundary: Simplex counting and Lipschitz covering argument; scientific utility depends on measuring family coverage, smoothness, and structural completeness.

costs.candidate_count: q=92,M=2 gives 4278 composition grid points; with 10 families this is 42780 candidate energies.
costs.deterministic_cover: A conservative simplex fill-distance bound h<=2(q-1)/M makes M>=4(q-1)L/eta sufficient; phase count grows combinatorially in q.
costs.random_cover: m scales as rho^-1*log(1/delta), where rho has a dimension-dependent factor (eta/L)^(q-1).

claims.falsifier: A measured phase family violates the claimed Lipschitz bound or a fully enumerated candidate set contradicts the asserted density/family-mass lower bound.
claims.next_gate: Estimate structural-family coverage and composition smoothness on a complete binary/ternary DFT benchmark; do not extrapolate to high-component systems without data.

claims.exact_statement: CAL is a Bayesian expected-information-gain policy over a finite candidate phase/composition grid; GNoME is a large learned generation/filter/DFT pipeline whose stability calls are relative to existing competitor databases. Neither source establishes global completeness against a phase outside its candidate/model information. A fair comparison must match training data, candidate universe/generator, DFT budget, target functional, and acquisition cost.
assumptions: Source-reported CAL/GNoME numbers refer to the cited papers' evaluation settings and are not reproduced here.
Equal-informed comparison freezes all policies before hidden labels and charges candidate generation and high-fidelity relaxations.
PBE/r2SCAN validation remains model evidence unless matched-condition experiment is measured.
claims.novelty_boundary: No claim of outperforming CAL or GNoME; proposed hidden-phase benchmark is future work. Their average-case gains may be real under their priors, while the minimax lower bound remains under the stated adversarial interface.

costs.CAL: Paper reports finite-grid ternary simulation with 66 compositions, 3 phases, 198 pairs, 40 synthetic energy surfaces, and 200 hull samples/10 hypothetical outcomes per EIG estimate.
costs.GNoME: Paper reports >10^9 candidates over the process, 2.2 million stable relative to previous databases, 381000 new updated-hull entries, 736 experimental matches; generator, training and DFT data are costs/information.
costs.experiment: No benchmark, synthesis, or outside validation executed.

claims.falsifier: Primary paper source contradicts the stated scope or an equal-budget frozen benchmark demonstrates a globally valid guarantee despite the one-hidden-ID oracle assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Execute the registered hidden-A2B benchmark and a physical Gibbs-energy falsifier; report false-global-stable rate, coverage, DFT core-hours, generator cost, and synthesis detection rate.

model_versus_nature: All deterministic statements certify only the named energy/free-energy intervals. DFT-to-experiment uniform error bounds, finite-temperature corrections, and synthesis detection floors remain UNKNOWN.
diagnostic_scope: Exact rational verification of one A2B fixture, two simplex counts, and sample-count examples only; not theorem proof or DFT validation.
